problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14129388/assets/eb4ea276f4b876ce42b3701d60c1a5967769b62b328c16e9f9e75ef050f18d6f.png)

A plate occupies the region $D$ enclosed by the $y$-axis and the curves $y={x}^{2}$ and $y=x+2$ in the first quadrant, as shown above. If the mass density function of $D$ is given by $\lambda (x,y)=15x,$ find the moment of inertia of the lamina about the $y$-axis.
worked_solution:
For a plane lamina $D$ with mass density function $\lambda (x,y),$ we have the following definitions:

- The moment of inertia about the $x$-axis is given by

$$
{I}_{x}={∬}_{D}{y}^{2}\lambda (x,y)\,\text{d}A.
$$

- The moment of inertia about the $y$-axis is given by

$$
{I}_{y}={∬}_{D}{x}^{2}\lambda (x,y)\,\text{d}A.
$$

- The moment of inertia about the origin is given by

$$
{I}_{0}={∬}_{D}({x}^{2}+{y}^{2})\lambda (x,y)\,\text{d}A={I}_{x}+{I}_{y}.
$$

First, notice that $D$ is a type I region with representation

$$
D=\{(x,y)\,:\,0\le x\le 2,\,\,{x}^{2}\le y\le x+2\},
$$

as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14129388/assets/f11f3026c9cc7f315781470791f03d3df97d7f292f8b713a1903f021bd5bf6c6.png)

Using the formula for ${I}_{y},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{I}_{y} & ={∬}_{D}{x}^{2}\lambda (x,y)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{{x}^{2}}^{x+2}{x}^{2}(15x)\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}[{\int }_{{x}^{2}}^{x+2}15{x}^{3}\,\text{d}y]\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}15{x}^{3}[y]_{y={x}^{2}}^{y=x+2}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}15{x}^{3}(x+2-{x}^{2})\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}15{x}^{4}+30{x}^{3}-15{x}^{5}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={[3{x}^{5}+\frac{15}{2}{x}^{4}-\frac{5}{2}{x}^{6}]}_{0}^{2} \\  & =96+120-160 \\  & =56.\end{aligned}
$$

A plate occupies the region D enclosed by the y-axis and the curves y=x2 and y=x+2 in the first quadrant, as shown above. If the mass density function of D is given by λ(x,y)=15x, find the moment of inertia of the lamina about the y-axis.

EXPLANATION

For a plane lamina D with mass density function λ(x,y), we have the following definitions:

  • The moment of inertia about the x-axis is given by Ix=∬Dy2λ(x,y)dA.

  • The moment of inertia about the y-axis is given by Iy=∬Dx2λ(x,y)dA.

  • The moment of inertia about the origin is given by I0=∬D(x2+y2)λ(x,y)dA=Ix+Iy.

First, notice that D is a type I region with representation

D={(x,y):0≤x≤2,x2≤y≤x+2},

as shown below.

Using the formula for Iy, we get

Iy=∬Dx2λ(x,y)dA=∫02∫x2x+2x2(15x)dydx=∫02[∫x2x+215x3dy]dx=∫0215x3[y]y=x2y=x+2dx=∫0215x3(x+2−x2)dx=∫0215x4+30x3−15x5dx=[3x5+152x4−52x6]02=96+120−160=56.
